outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the Berge conjecture has not been settled in its knot-level form: the only substantive in-window development is the tunnel-number-one case proved by Li, Moriah and Pinsky (first posted January 2017, revised to v7 on 1 November 2024, published in Geometry & Topology in 2025), which shows that a tunnel-number-one knot in S³ with a nontrivial lens space surgery is doubly primitive, and no source I found credits an AI system with any part of the mathematics on this problem.
problem_asks: Read from the statement alone. (a) A universal claim over all knots K in S³: no restriction on tunnel number, genus, fibredness or hyperbolicity is stated. (b) Hypothesis: K admits a Dehn surgery, at any slope, that yields a lens space. (c) Conclusion: K is a Berge knot, meaning a knot in S³ that lies on a genus-two Heegaard surface and is primitive in each of the two handlebodies (doubly primitive); Berge’s twelve families are the known examples. (d) The word ‘only’ asserts one inclusion, lens-space-surgery knots ⊆ Berge knots. The converse (Berge knots have lens space surgeries) is part of Berge’s construction and is not what the bullet asks. (e) The bullet does not say ‘non-trivial’. The unknot has lens space surgeries, so its status against the bullet depends on convention; Li–Moriah–Pinsky state their version for non-trivial knots. (f) The bullet does not restrict the slope to integers. The cyclic surgery theorem reduces non-integral lens space surgeries to torus knots, which are already known cases.

events.what_happened: Ozsváth and Szabó, ‘On knot Floer homology and lens space surgeries’ (arXiv math/0303017). Using knot Floer restrictions, stronger than their earlier absolute-grading restrictions, and combining them with Berge’s constructions, they classify the lens spaces L(p,q) that arise as integral surgeries on knots in S³ with |p| ≤ 1500. Stated side consequences: sharp four-ball genus bounds for Berge knots, and all nonzero Alexander polynomial coefficients of such knots are ±1. Journal: Topology 44 (2005) 1281–1300, per a search listing (journal page not opened).
events.revisions: v1 2 Mar 2003; v2 2 Mar 2004 (current on the arXiv abstract page).
events.delivers: Lens-space level only. For |p| ≤ 1500, the lens spaces realised as integral surgeries on S³ knots are exactly those realised by Berge knots. It restricts the knots (Alexander coefficients ±1) but identifies no knot and says nothing about lens spaces with |p| > 1500.
events.remains: Every lens space with |p| > 1500; the knot-level question of whether every S³ knot with a lens space surgery is a Berge knot.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2005, per a search listing; the journal page was not opened

events.time_since_posted: Published 2005; no later engagement specific to this result was searched for.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture at the lens-space level. No counterexample; no knot-level claim.

events.what_happened: Yi Ni, ‘Knot Floer homology detects fibred knots’ (arXiv math/0607156). Proves the Ozsváth–Szabó conjecture for null-homologous knots in closed 3-manifolds. Corollary stated on the abstract page: if a knot in S³ admits a lens space surgery, then the knot is fibred. Later versions say ‘to appear in Inventiones Mathematicae’.
events.revisions: v1 6 Jul 2006; v2 17 Jul 2006; v3 7 Oct 2006; v4 15 Sep 2007 (‘incorporates referee’s suggestions, to appear in Inventiones Mathematicae’). The arXiv page gives DOI 10.1007/s00222-007-0075-9; the journal page was not opened.
events.delivers: A constraint: every S³ knot with a lens space surgery is fibred. It establishes fibredness only and identifies no knot.
events.remains: Which knots have lens space surgeries; the full conjecture.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted after referee suggestions, per the v4 comment; the journal page was not opened

events.time_since_posted: Journal version to appear 2007; cited by Li–Moriah–Pinsky’s introduction as the fibredness result.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; a constraint on lens-space-surgery knots.

events.what_happened: Ichihara and Saito, ‘Lens spaces obtainable by surgery on doubly primitive knots’ (arXiv 0708.3347). Gives an algorithm for deciding whether a given lens space arises from Berge’s surgery on a doubly primitive knot, and a complete characterisation of such surgeries that yield lens spaces containing Klein bottles. Journal: Algebr. Geom. Topol. 7 (2007) 1949–1962.
events.delivers: Concerns only surgeries on doubly primitive (Berge) knots: which lens spaces they yield and the Klein-bottle case. A search summary reports that no hyperbolic doubly primitive knot gives such a surgery; that was not checked in the text. Says nothing about knots outside the Berge list.
events.remains: Everything about knots that are not already doubly primitive, which is the conjecture’s content.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (2007), per the arXiv journal reference

events.direction: Neutral to the conjecture. It is about the Berge knots only.

events.what_happened: Matthew Hedden, ‘On Floer homology and the Berge conjecture on knots admitting lens space surgeries’ (arXiv 0710.0357). Completes step one of a two-part programme proposed with Baker and Grigsby: a knot in a lens space with a three-sphere surgery has simple (rank-minimal) knot Floer homology. Step two is conjectural: for a fixed lens space, the only knots with simple knot Floer homology form a small finite family. Hedden verifies step two for one family, using results of Baker. Gives a Floer-homology proof of a theorem of Berge. With Ni’s work, these knots form the first infinite family of nontrivial knots characterised by their knot Floer homology. Journal: Trans. AMS 363 (2011) 949–968, per a search listing (AMS page not opened).
events.delivers: A restriction on knots in lens spaces with S³ surgeries (simple knot Floer homology), applied to dual knots. A family-level verification of the conjectural step two. No general identification of knots.
events.remains: Step two in general, and the knot-level conjecture for all knots.

checked_by.who: Transactions of the AMS (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2011, per a search listing

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; a partial result, with step two left conjectural.

events.what_happened: Joshua Greene, ‘The lens space realization problem’ (arXiv 1010.6257; Annals of Mathematics 177 (2013) 449–511, per a search listing). The arXiv text states: Theorem 1.2: if positive integer surgery on K ⊂ L(p,q) yields S³, then K lies in the same homology class as a Berge knot B ⊂ L(p,q). Theorem 1.3: if K ⊂ S³ has a lens space surgery K_p, there is a Berge knot B ⊂ S³ with B_p ≅ K_p and HFK(B) ≅ HFK(K); furthermore every doubly primitive knot in S³ is a Berge knot. The text states the Berge conjecture as Conjecture 1.1 and says an affirmative answer ‘would settle Moser’s original question’.
events.delivers: Lens-space level: the lens spaces obtained by integral surgery on S³ knots are exactly those obtained from Berge knots, with matching knot Floer homology. Knot level: only that every doubly primitive knot in S³ is a Berge knot. By the paper’s own statement of Conjecture 1.1, it does not show that every S³ knot with a lens space surgery is a Berge knot. Li–Moriah–Pinsky’s footnote claims otherwise (see disputes).
events.remains: Whether every S³ knot with a lens space surgery is a Berge knot (Conjecture 1.1 in Greene’s text).

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2013, per a search listing (Annals page not opened)

events.time_since_posted: Published 2013; cited by Jo–Park–Park (2024) and Guo (2026), and by Li–Moriah–Pinsky.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture at the lens-space level. The knot-level statement is left open in the text.

events.what_happened: Baker, Buck and Lecuona, ‘Some knots in S¹×S² with lens space surgeries’ (arXiv 1302.7011). Proposes a classification of knots in S¹×S² with longitudinal lens space surgeries (Berge–Gabai knots, knots on fibres of genus-one fibred knots, and sporadic knots), and conjectures that these form the complete list of doubly primitive knots in S¹×S². A search summary reports later publication in Communications in Analysis and Geometry (2016); not verified.
events.revisions: v1 27 Feb 2013 only (per the arXiv abstract page).
events.delivers: A conjecture about S¹×S², a different manifold. No result about knots in S³.
events.remains: The S¹×S² completeness claim, whose tunnel-number-one case Li–Moriah–Pinsky say they resolve for S²×S¹. Nothing for S³.
events.time_since_posted: Li–Moriah–Pinsky’s abstract says their result resolves a conjecture of Greene and of Baker, Buck and Lecuona for tunnel number one knots in S²×S¹.
events.direction: No direction for S³. This is a conjecture for a different manifold.

events.what_happened: Greene and Ni, ‘Non-simple genus minimizers in lens spaces’ (arXiv 1305.0517). Constructs many non-simple rational genus minimisers in lens spaces, answering a question of Rasmussen negatively. A talk abstract by Greene says the lens-space genus question is ‘closely connected with the Berge conjecture’. The paper is about lens spaces, not S³ knots.
events.revisions: Not checked. The month is taken from the arXiv identifier (1305) and a Caltech listing.
events.delivers: Rational genus minimisers in lens spaces. This is not a statement about S³ knots with lens space surgeries.
events.remains: Everything in the bullet, as far as this paper is concerned.
events.direction: Neighbouring. No direction on the bullet.

events.what_happened: Baker, Doleshal and Hoffman, ‘On manifolds with multiple lens space fillings’ (arXiv 1308.5002). The abstract states that it shows ‘the doubly primitive knots in S³ and S¹×S² have no unexpected extra lens space surgery’. The paper’s main subject is 3-manifolds with several lens space fillings and the sharpness of the cyclic surgery bound.
events.delivers: About the surgeries of the doubly primitive (Berge) knots themselves: no lens space surgery beyond the expected ones. It says nothing about knots outside the Berge list.
events.remains: Everything about knots that are not doubly primitive.
events.time_since_posted: Li–Moriah–Pinsky cite it as a theorem (per a search summary of their text; not confirmed in the text read). No separate reading found.
events.direction: Neutral to the conjecture. It is about the Berge knots only.

events.what_happened: Baker and Hoffman, ‘The Poincaré homology sphere, lens space surgeries, and some knots with tunnel number two’ (arXiv 1504.06682). Exhibits an infinite family of tunnel-number-two knots in the Poincaré homology sphere P with integral lens space surgeries. The paper notes that these knots are not doubly primitive, and they are counterexamples to several conjectures stated for P. Appendix by Hoffman on hyperbolic knots in P. Journal: Pacific J. Math. 305 (2020) 1–27.
events.delivers: Shows that the doubly-primitive picture of lens space surgeries fails in P. It establishes nothing for S³ knots, and it is not a counterexample to the S³ statement.

checked_by.who: Pacific Journal of Mathematics (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2020, per the arXiv journal reference

events.direction: Counterexamples to the analogue in P. No direction for S³, which is the bullet’s setting.
events.object: An explicit family K_n in the Poincaré homology sphere P, one for each integer n, with an integral surgery to the lens space L(3n²+n+1, −3n+2). The paper states tunnel number 2 for |n| ≥ 4 and that the knots are not doubly primitive. The formula comes from a search summary of the paper and was not checked in the text. Explicit, not an existence proof.

events.what_happened: Abigail Thompson, ‘Dehn surgery on complicated fibered knots in the 3-sphere’ (arXiv 1604.04902). For a fibred knot K ⊂ S³ with sufficiently complicated monodromy, no Dehn surgery yields a lens space. The arXiv page notes that, combined with Ni’s result, a knot with a lens space surgery is fibred and has relatively simple monodromy.
events.delivers: A constraint on the monodromy of fibred knots that have lens space surgeries. It identifies no knots.
events.remains: Which knots have lens space surgeries, and whether simple monodromy forces a Berge knot.
events.time_since_posted: No journal version or engagement found in the searches; not checked specifically.
events.direction: Partial and consistent: a constraint on knots that have lens space surgeries.

events.what_happened: Tao Li, Yoav Moriah and Tali Pinsky, ‘Tunnel number one knots satisfy the Berge conjecture’ (arXiv 1701.01421; Geom. Topol. 29:6 (2025) 3271–3343). Main theorem (Theorem 7, per a summary of the html text): for a tunnel number one knot K in M, where M is S³ or (S²×S¹)#L(r,s), with irreducible exterior, if some nontrivial Dehn surgery on K yields a lens space then K is doubly primitive in M. The abstract says: ‘For M = S³ this resolves the tunnel number one Berge Conjecture. For M = S²×S¹ this resolves a conjecture of Greene and Baker, Buck and Lecuona for tunnel number one knots.’ Their Conjecture 2 is the full Berge conjecture (a non-trivial knot K ⊂ S³ with a Dehn surgery to a lens space is doubly primitive). Their Conjecture 3 is the tunnel-number-one case, which they prove. The first posting (v1, 5 Jan 2017) was by Moriah and Pinsky alone, titled ‘The Berge Conjecture for tunnel number one knots’; its abstract says that a tunnel number one knot K ⊂ S³ with a Dehn filling giving a lens space is in the Berge list.
events.revisions: v1 5 Jan 2017 (Moriah and Pinsky; title ‘The Berge Conjecture for tunnel number one knots’); v2 28 Feb 2017; v3 17 Sep 2018, listed as withdrawn (1 KB); v4 14 Dec 2019; v5 4 Apr 2023; v6 6 Apr 2023; v7 1 Nov 2024 (current; first author Tao Li; title ‘Tunnel number one knots satisfy the Berge Conjecture’; adds the S²×S¹ part). Journal: received 2 Aug 2023, revised 17 Aug 2024, accepted 31 Oct 2024, published 22 Sep 2025 (msp.org metadata). The in-window dates are the v7 revision (1 Nov 2024), acceptance (31 Oct 2024) and publication (22 Sep 2025). The date of the first public written argument is the 2017 posting, per §5.1.
events.delivers: For knots K ⊂ S³ of tunnel number one (in the paper’s sense) with a nontrivial lens space surgery: K is doubly primitive, i.e. a Berge knot. The S²×S¹ results are outside this bullet. The ‘irreducible exterior’ hypothesis appears in v7 but not in the v1 abstract. My own reasoning, not stated in the paper: for a knot in S³ the exterior is always irreducible (a sphere in the exterior separates S³ with the connected knot on one side, so it bounds a ball in the exterior), so the hypothesis narrows nothing for S³ knots.
events.remains: Knots in S³ of tunnel number two or more with a lens space surgery. The full knot-level conjecture (Conjecture 2 in the paper).

checked_by.who: Geometry & Topology (journal of record) and its referee
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal; the acknowledgements thank ‘the referee’
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted 31 Oct 2024 and published 22 Sep 2025 after refereeing, per the journal metadata

events.time_since_posted: First posted about 9 years 9 months before 11 Oct 2026. Published in G&T about 13 months before that date. No 2025–2026 paper citing it was found in the searches.

withdrawn.what: arXiv v3 (17 Sep 2018) is listed as withdrawn (1 KB); v4 (14 Dec 2019) restores the paper’s text.

events.direction: In the direction the Berge conjecture asserts: lens-space-surgery knots are Berge knots. Proved for the tunnel-number-one class only. No counterexample reported.

events.what_happened: John Berge, ‘Some knots with surgeries yielding lens spaces’ (arXiv 1802.09722). A facsimile of Berge’s circa-1990 unpublished manuscript, with text reset in TeX and figures redrawn. The families of knots with lens space surgeries that it describes are the origin of the twelve families (Berge knots) named in Wikipedia and Greene. Per a search summary, its Theorem 1 characterises these knots as curves on the boundary of a genus-two handlebody. The arXiv text was not read.
events.revisions: v1 27 Feb 2018 only (17 pages, 10 figures, 1 table). The mathematics dates from circa 1990, but nothing was public before this posting.
events.delivers: The existence side: lens space surgeries on Berge’s families. Completeness, which is the conjecture’s content, is attributed to Berge in secondary sources but is not stated in the abstract I read.
events.remains: Completeness of the list, which is the open question.
events.time_since_posted: Not checked beyond the abstract page.
events.direction: Constructive: the list of families that realise lens spaces. Consistent with the conjecture as the list.
events.object: The families of knots in S³ (Berge’s knots) that lie on a genus-two Heegaard surface and yield lens spaces by surgery. Described at the family level; the abstract gives no explicit example. Explicit families, not existence proofs.

events.what_happened: Davies, Juhász, Lackenby and Tomašev, ‘The signature and cusp geometry of hyperbolic knots’ (arXiv 2111.15323; Geom. Topol. 28 (2024) 2313–2343). Introduces the natural slope of a hyperbolic knot in S³ and proves an inequality between twice the signature and the natural slope, with an error of a constant times volume over the cube of the injectivity radius. Abstract: ‘This inequality was discovered using machine learning to detect relationships between various knot invariants.’ Stated application: ‘to Dehn surgery and to 4-ball genus’. Neither the abstract nor the introduction text I read mentions lens spaces or the Berge conjecture.
events.delivers: An inequality for hyperbolic knots, with applications to Dehn surgery in general. No lens-space or Berge statement that I found.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2024, per the arXiv journal reference (journal page not opened)

events.direction: Neighbouring. No direction on the bullet.

events.what_happened: Jo, Park and Park, ‘On lens spaces bounding smooth 4-manifolds with b₂=1’ (arXiv 2410.22719; Algebr. Geom. Topol. 26 (2026) 2659–2688). A lens space paper, not a paper about knots. Its introduction restates Greene’s theorem as lens space realisation. It states the Berge conjecture as its Conjecture 2.7, at the lens-space level: ‘If an integer surgery along a knot K in S³ produces a lens space, then it must arise from Berge’s construction.’ It says Greene’s result ‘confirms “half” of the Berge conjecture’, without saying which half.
events.revisions: v1 30 Oct 2024; v2 12 Nov 2024; v3 30 Sep 2026 (final version, per the comments field).
events.delivers: Nothing new about the Berge conjecture. A restatement of Greene’s theorem with the ‘half’ description.
events.remains: All of the conjecture, as its own Conjecture 2.7 states it at the lens-space level, and the knot-level statement of the bullet.
events.direction: None. A restatement of Greene’s theorem with the ‘half’ description.

events.what_happened: GitHub issue #2167, ‘Berge Conjecture (Dehn Surgery and Lens Spaces)’, in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures. Opened 4 Feb 2026 by GitHub user franzhusch; state open; labels include ‘wikipedia’ and ‘new conjecture’. Natural-language statement: ‘If a knot K ⊂ S³ admits a non-trivial Dehn surgery producing a lens space, then K is a Berge knot.’ The issue has no comments and no linked pull requests, and it contains no Lean statement. It says the description ‘may contain subtle errors’, and its body says: ‘This issue was generated by an AI agent and reviewed by me.’
events.delivers: Nothing mathematical. It is a statement of the conjecture, with no proof and no progress.
events.time_since_posted: No comments since opening. ‘Reviewed by me’ is the issue author’s own statement, not an external check.

events.what_happened: Qilong Guo, ‘Lens Space Surgeries and the Bleiler–Litherland Conjecture’ (arXiv 2609.31757; single author; 9 pages). Claims a proof that every lens space obtained by nontrivial Dehn surgery on a hyperbolic knot in S³ has order at least 18. Key ingredient, per the abstract: if a hyperbolic knot K of genus g admits a lens space surgery with slope ±(4g−2), then its Alexander polynomial has a real root outside the unit circle. Also uses Floer restrictions, Gabai and Gabai–Oertel, and Ni’s fixed-point theorem. The introduction cites Berge’s conjecture and Greene’s theorem; the proof of Corollary 1.5 uses Greene’s theorem to obtain a knot from Berge’s list. The abstract does not mention Berge.
events.revisions: v1 26 Sep 2026; v2 30 Sep 2026: ‘A minor issue in the proof was corrected; the main results are unchanged.’
events.delivers: A restriction on the orders of lens space surgeries on hyperbolic knots (order at least 18). It identifies no knots and does not show that any S³ knot with a lens space surgery is a Berge knot.
events.remains: The Berge conjecture. The order question is a different problem.

checked_by.qualification: Named in the acknowledgements. Qualifications not verified in my sources
checked_by.what_they_did: Pointed out an issue with the argument in an earlier version of Lemma 2.7; v2 corrected it (per the acknowledgements and the v2 comment)

events.doubts: A single-author preprint, not refereed. The only external engagement recorded is one error in an earlier version of Lemma 2.7, reported by Sivek and corrected in v2. No outstanding error is reported.
events.direction: Neighbouring. It cuts in the direction of the Bleiler–Litherland conjecture. No direction on Berge.

disputes.summary: Whether Greene’s 2010/2013 theorem completes the knot-level Berge conjecture. Li–Moriah–Pinsky’s introduction, footnote 2, says: ‘Ultimately the proof that Berge’s list for knots in S³ is complete is a consequence of J. Greene’s Lens space realization paper (see [19]).’ Greene’s text states the Berge conjecture as Conjecture 1.1 and says an affirmative answer ‘would settle Moser’s original question’. It proves the lens-space-level Theorems 1.2–1.3 and the statement that every doubly primitive knot in S³ is a Berge knot. Li–Moriah–Pinsky themselves state the full conjecture as their Conjecture 2 and prove only the tunnel-number-one case. Wikipedia’s Berge knot article (cached page, last edited 24 July 2022) says progress has been slow and does not claim completion. The footnote conflicts with the other sources. I have not resolved it.

What ‘confirms half of the Berge conjecture’ means. Jo–Park–Park (arXiv 2410.22719, first posted 30 Oct 2024, inside the window) say Greene’s result ‘confirms “half” of the Berge conjecture’ without saying which half. Their own Conjecture 2.7 is the lens-space-level statement, which Greene’s Theorems 1.2–1.3 address. The bullet’s knot-level statement is the one Greene’s Conjecture 1.1 leaves open. The ‘half’ description is not supported by the knot-level reading.

Whether the irreducible-exterior hypothesis narrows the tunnel-number-one class in the bullet’s setting (S³). The v7 abstract requires an irreducible exterior; the v1 (2017) abstract does not mention it. My reasoning, not stated in the paper: for a knot in S³ the exterior is always irreducible, so the hypothesis is vacuous for S³ knots. The judging pass should check this against the paper’s text, which I did not read in full.

summary: Searches (47 web searches plus about 40 page fetches) found no source that settles the Berge conjecture as stated, and no source that credits an AI system with any of the mathematics on it. The one substantive development inside the window is the tunnel-number-one case. Li, Moriah and Pinsky’s preprint (arXiv 1701.01421) was first posted on 5 January 2017 by Moriah and Pinsky alone under the title ‘The Berge Conjecture for tunnel number one knots’. Version v7 (1 Nov 2024) carries the final authorship and title; the paper was accepted by Geometry & Topology on 31 Oct 2024 and published there on 22 Sep 2025 (vol. 29, no. 6, pp. 3271–3343, DOI 10.2140/gt.2025.29.3271). It proves that a tunnel-number-one knot in S³ with a nontrivial lens space surgery is doubly primitive, which is the Berge-knot conclusion. Per §5.1 I dated the event to the 2017 first posting, so the in-window items are the v7 revision, the acceptance and the 2025 publication. The full knot-level conjecture is not resolved in any source I read, and the paper itself states it separately as Conjecture 2. Close calls: (1) whether a restricted class counts toward a conjecture about all knots; I record the restriction as it stands. (2) Footnote 2 of the Li–Moriah–Pinsky introduction says Greene’s paper makes Berge’s list complete for S³ knots, but Greene’s own text leaves the conjecture open and Li–Moriah–Pinsky state the full conjecture separately; I have recorded this as a dispute, not resolved it. (3) Jo–Park–Park (October 2024, in the window) say Greene’s result ‘confirms half’ of the conjecture without saying which half. Pre-window results recorded: Ozsváth–Szabó 2003 (lens spaces with |p| ≤ 1500), Ni 2006 (lens-space-surgery knots are fibred), Ichihara–Saito 2007, Hedden 2007 (first step of a Floer programme, second step conjectural), Greene 2010/2013 (lens-space level), Baker–Buck–Lecuona 2013 (an S¹×S² conjecture), Baker–Doleshal–Hoffman 2013, Greene–Ni 2013, Baker–Hoffman 2015 (Poincaré-sphere counterexamples, not S³), Thompson 2016 (monodromy constraint), Berge’s manuscript (posted 2018). Neighbouring in-window or recent events, recorded as discounted: Jo–Park–Park 2024 (restatement); Guo 2026 (Bleiler–Litherland for hyperbolic knots; disclosed AI use limited to language polishing); a DeepMind formal-conjectures issue (4 Feb 2026) whose body says it was ‘generated by an AI agent and reviewed by me’, a statement only. The AI searches (queries naming Claude, GPT, Gemini, AlphaEvolve, DeepMind, OpenAI, machine learning and Lean) found no AI-credited mathematics on this conjecture. The natural-slope paper (2021) used machine learning to find an inequality, but nothing in its text connects it to lens spaces. The Wikipedia article is cached from 2022 and lists no 2024–2026 references. ‘Berge conjecture’ also names a graph-theory problem (perfect graphs; Berge–Fulkerson), which I excluded as a different problem. The date line printed on the Li–Moriah–Pinsky HTML is unreliable: one fetch read ‘August 9, 2026’, another ‘August 24, 2026’, against an arXiv v7 stamp of 1 Nov 2024. I have not resolved it.
competing_reading: Read the window as containing the settling event. Taken at face value, footnote 2 of Li–Moriah–Pinsky says Greene’s 2010 paper already gives completeness for S³ knots. On that reading the problem was resolved in 2010, outside the window, and the 2024–2025 papers are re-confirmations. The opposite reading, which the paper’s own Conjecture 2 supports, is that only the tunnel-number-one class is proved and the full conjecture is open. A third reading treats Jo–Park–Park’s ‘confirms half’ as an in-window status claim; the text does not support it, because the half is not identified and their Conjecture 2.7 is at the lens-space level.
what_would_settle_it: (a) Greene’s Annals text: whether Conjecture 1.1 is claimed proved anywhere, and how Theorem 1.3 is stated for knots in S³. (b) The full context of Li–Moriah–Pinsky footnote 2 and their reference [19] in the Geometry & Topology version. (c) A 2025–2026 survey, or a statement by Greene, Ni or Hedden, on whether the knot-level conjecture is open. (d) The printed date on the G&T / arXiv v7 PDF, to settle the 1 Nov 2024 stamp against the ‘August 2026’ date lines. (e) The v1 (2017) text, to confirm whether the tunnel-number-one claim and its hypotheses changed between v1 and v7. (f) A 2026 paper on knots of tunnel number two or more with lens space surgeries, or an explicit citation of Li–Moriah–Pinsky in that area.

judgement.why: The only event that settles part of the knot-level statement is Li–Moriah–Pinsky's tunnel-number-one case: a case, digested via Geometry & Topology acceptance. Its first public argument for S³ is the January 2017 posting (v1 abstract already claims the S³ tunnel-number-one result); v7 (Nov 2024) added the S²×S¹ part and authorship changes, not the S³ mathematics in question, so it is pre-snapshot. The v3 withdrawal was reversed by v4 and the paper was refereed, so it is not knocked down. Lens-space-level results (Ozsváth–Szabó, Greene) answer a changed question — which lens spaces arise, not which knots — so they are variants; Greene's footnote-2 dispute is answered by Greene's own Conjecture 1.1 and LMP's Conjecture 2 leaving the knot-level statement open. Constraints (Ni fibredness, Thompson monodromy, Hedden step one) settle no restriction of the question and are none. Results in S¹×S², the Poincaré sphere or other lens spaces are variants. In-window items are a restatement (Jo–Park–Park), an AI-generated issue stating the conjecture (no mathematics), and Guo's Bleiler–Litherland result (a different question; AI use limited to language polishing, systems empty). The natural-slope paper's machine learning concerns an unrelated inequality and no system is listed.
judgement.doubts: Close call on li-moriah-pinsky-2017 dating: the v1 text was not read beyond its abstract and v3 was withdrawn, so if the S³ argument materially changed by v7 the event could be re-dated to Nov 2024 (it would then be an in-window, digested case). The record supports the 2017 date since the v1 abstract states the same S³ claim. Greene's 'every doubly primitive knot in S³ is a Berge knot' was treated as part of a variant/lens-space event, not a case of the bullet.
